factorized_domain_proof.recurrence: For each participating check c, XOR residual position sets to P_c. Every |P_c|-subset of its six qubits occurs, each in |P_c|!(6-|P_c|)! local permutations. Split check factors L,R; count pairs with equal 72-bit syndrome and unequal full 84-bit signature. Exact support-domain count is sum_s L_low[s]R_low[s] - sum_v L_full[v]R_full[v]. Multiply by the per-support permutation factors.
factorized_domain_proof.zero_domain_rule: A zero exact count means only that this fixed candidate selector has empty local-order validity domain and is discarded; it is not absence evidence for schedules or other mechanisms.

limitations: Local-order domain nonemptiness alone does not assert extendability to a legal global frozen schedule. A separate exact frozen-CNF strict-expansion query is required before pre-outer installation.
No zero-domain result is interpreted as a global absence statement.
Pairwise GF(2) synthesis is tested only for the complete pair family among the 164 prior selectors; higher-arity GF(2) combinations are outside this finite test.
theorem: Every retained ordinary selector fixes at most ten distinct direct-360 columns. Its exact predicate is true exactly on the factorized local-order domain recorded here; on every such tuple the named canonical mechanism has zero 72-bit syndrome and a nonzero 12-bit logical vector. Replacing R:check:0 canonical positions {0,1} by physical suffix {2,3,4,5} changes support by the full same-sector stabilizer row, while kinds 1 and 2 agree, so the explicit named physical mechanism is valid throughout the same domain.
